segments.title: Sasebo's island channels as a fighting environment
segments.summary: A cruise through the islands around Sasebo shows how confined channels, visible rocks, and restricted movement make the local geography difficult for naval combat.
segments.body: The harbour cruise winds through islands and narrow channels around Sasebo, giving a direct view of a crowded coastal operating area. The area is described as a poor place to choose for a battle because rocks and restricted water limit movement. Close-range action might exploit the confined space, but a force would have little room to disengage or manoeuvre. Submarines face an especially awkward problem because rocks are visible near the route and leave little safe space for submerged navigation. The discussion also considers whether a smaller vessel could combine enough firepower with the speed and handling needed to get through trouble. Coastal geography therefore constrains ship choice, weapon use, and freedom of movement.

evidence.note: The speakers describe the island cruise, the area's battle history, constrained fighting space, and the visible rocks that make it hazardous for submarines.
The discussion contrasts firepower with the speed and manoeuvrability needed to get through the confined waters.
